text:
jamie: We should do a canonical quant sweep for FP8 / INT4 ahead of the next Dedicated rollout. Can't compare apples-to-oranges without a single config source.

ravi: Agreed. Quick clarity — what needs locking in the canonical config?

jamie: Model artifact (exact binary hash), quant profile file, KV-cache warm/cold flag, attention block size, allocator settings, and batching curve + sampling seed. Also record prompt template variant.

sasha: And capture both intrinsic and extrinsic signals. Intrinsic: lm-qa, tokenwise-snr, perplexity proxies. Extrinsic: chat-sat p95, hallucination-rate, formatting regressions. Break them out by prompt-length buckets (short/medium/long).

maria: I can wire a 10% shadow route for 24h to collect live signals. For heavy offline sweeps, we should use the bench cluster.

alex: Throttle shadow concurrency per-GPU to avoid impacting Dedicated pools. Bench runs should use the same allocator to match memory behavior.

jamie: Output artifact (small JSON) per-profile should include: profile_name, baseline_profile, sample_count, deg_score_delta, hallucination_delta, latency_p95_delta, mem_margin_mb, regression_examples[]. Upload to S3 and hand URL to quality-orch.

sasha: regression_examples[] must be tiny (<=8). Each example: input, baseline_out, candidate_out, short_diff, tag (hallucination|omission|format|toxicity).

ravi: What's the deg_score formula? Teams will implement it differently unless we standardize.

sasha: Proposal: deg_score = 0.6*lm_qa_drop + 0.25*anchor_fail_rate + 0.15*token_snr_drop. We should publish exact metric definitions and thresholds.

jamie: Gate proposal: fail the profile if any of: deg_score increase > 1.5, hallucination-rate increase > 0.5% absolute, latency_p95 increase > 25ms OR >12% (whichever larger). On fail -> pick INT8-compat fallback for rollout.

maria: Add memory safety rule: if average mem_margin_mb < 200 then mark profile as "risky" and require additional canary validation. INT4 kernels sometimes need extra workspace; capture peak and avg.

ravi: Runtime integration: we need a compatibility checker the orch uses before swapping a profile. Checker should compare model header fields: arch, dim, kv-format, quant-schema-version. If mismatch -> abort.

alex: Also define what "compatible variant" means: mapping table for quant formats (e.g., fp8-e4m3 -> int8 per-channel mapping) and a canonical filename scheme so orchestration can pick fallbacks deterministically.

jamie: Automation: canary rollout plan: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 2h holds. At each stage run quick sanity: deg_score sample (N=500), latency p95, and mem anomalies. Auto-rollback on gate breach.

sasha: For observability, add per-customer slices and user-agent buckets (mobile/web) — many issues only surface on mobile clients or longctx >2048.

maria: I'll tag big customers to opt-out of aggressive FP8 unless they opt-in. Also will cap concurrency: 30 QPS per pool for shadow.

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-6482: "canonical-quant-sweep + canary readiness". Assignees: maria (shadow routing), jamie (sweep runner), sasha (metrics spec), alex (rollout automation). ETA 5d. :white_check_mark:

jamie: Action items:
- maria: implement shadow split + concurrency caps (ETA 2d)
- jamie: author canonical config + run offline bench sweep (ETA 3d)
- sasha: publish deg_score spec and regression_examples schema (ETA 2d)
- alex: implement canary automation and compatibility checks (ETA 4d)

ravi: One last item: include a small regression artifact pointer (S3) with up to 8 failed examples per profile so oncall can triage quickly.

jamie: Will do. I'll post S3 links here after the offline run.

maria: Queued bench job: bench-cluster/sweeps/1799991234-offline (ETA ~5h). I'll report back when complete.
